strengths: Addresses genuine problem of poor cross-dataset generalization in SOD through practical synthetic data approach
Creates large-scale high-quality synthetic dataset (139,981 images, 2x+ larger than existing SOD datasets combined) with demonstrated quality control
Strong empirical results with 20-30% MAE improvements in cross-dataset generalization and state-of-the-art performance across 7 benchmarks
Comprehensive experimental evaluation including extensive ablations (Tables 5-8) that validate each component and design choice
Thoughtful integration of multiple techniques: multi-modal diffusion, iterative feedback-driven generation, multi-stage quality filtering, and ambiguity-aware architecture
Thorough evaluation methodology with appropriate metrics for SOD and attention to reproducibility details
Effectively demonstrates that synthetic data training can match or exceed task-specific model performance
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty—mostly applies existing techniques (FLUX-DIT diffusion, DINO-v3 features, standard losses) with straightforward engineering rather than novel algorithmic contributions

Ambiguity-aware architecture central to contributions but insufficiently analyzed: unclear how often genuine ambiguity occurs vs. model uncertainty, what percentage of scenes need multi-masks, how masks are selected at inference, minimal ablation impact (Table 7)
Critical hyperparameter choices (λ_mask=10, λ_score=0.05, λ_reg=0.1, γ=0.2, ψ=0.8, β=0.5) lack justification and sensitivity analysis
Shallow dataset quality assessment: only 0.7% manually verified with suspiciously low defect rates (14 incomplete masks in 1,000 samples); no inter-annotator agreement or rigorous domain gap analysis

Missing computational cost analysis: iterative generation pipeline cost not discussed, inference time comparisons absent, S3OD has ~117M parameters (substantially more than some baselines) but efficiency trade-offs not addressed

Experimental design issues: no statistical significance testing, error bars, or confidence intervals; baseline models from different years (2019-2024); unclear capacity control across compared models; oracle evaluation somewhat unrealistic
No failure case analysis or identification of remaining limitations; missing discussion of edge cases and method failure modes
Insufficient comparison with recent synthetic SOD methods (MaskFactory, DatasetDM comparisons incomplete; missing head-to-head with other generative approaches)
Generalization scope limited to natural images with specific objects; no testing on out-of-distribution domains (medical, microscopy, thermal); unclear robustness to significant distribution shifts
Missing ablations on quality filtering components and their individual contributions; limited analysis of which filtering stages remove what percentage of samples

strengths: Large-scale synthetic dataset (139,981 images) substantially exceeding existing SOD datasets
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple benchmarks (DIS-5K, HR-SOD, DUT, DAVIS) with standard metrics
Well-engineered pipeline combining multi-modal diffusion with iterative feedback for continuous dataset improvement
Addresses genuine problem of data scarcity in pixel-precise annotation tasks
Thorough implementation details including detailed prompting strategy (Appendix A) and quality filtering procedures
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: model architecture combines existing components (DPT, DINO-v3, standard losses) without substantial innovation

Extraordinarily strong results (synthetic-only models outperform real-data trained models by 20-50%) lack adequate explanation and contradict established understanding of domain gap and distribution shift
Unfair experimental comparisons: S3OD trained on 139,981 images vs. baselines on smaller datasets; missing control of scaling existing methods to equivalent data volume
Evaluation methodology concerns: S3OD* variant uses oracle-like 'best match over three masks' advantage not applied to baseline methods; FID score of 1.74 appears unrealistically good
Insufficient analysis of dataset quality: 6.8% samples filtered out suggests systematic generation issues not adequately characterized; no systematic study of failure modes by object category
Lack of insights into why synthetic data enables such strong generalization; no investigation of when synthetic data helps vs. hurts
Iterative generation mechanism optimizing for IoU scores may introduce bias toward model-friendly cases rather than representative distributions

Reproducibility concerns: reliance on potentially unavailable FLUX-Krea checkpoint; no clear code/dataset release plan; many hyperparameters (α, β, γ, λ weights) appear arbitrary without sensitivity analysis
Limited visual analysis: only one qualitative comparison (Figure 8) on single dataset; insufficient evidence of quality across diverse scenarios
Missing fundamental ablations: what happens when scaling real datasets to 139,981 images? What design choices are essential vs. incidental?

strengths: Substantial dataset contribution: 139,981+ high-resolution images, more than 2x existing SOD datasets combined
Sophisticated multi-modal data generation pipeline combining FLUX DiFT, concept attention maps, and DINO-v3 features with iterative feedback for quality improvement
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple benchmarks (DIS, HR-SOD, UHRSD, DUTS, DUT-OMRON) with strong cross-dataset generalization results (20.5-46.7% MAE improvements)
Thoughtful multi-mask decoder architecture for handling inherent ambiguity in salient object detection
Thorough ablation studies (Tables 5-8) demonstrating contribution of each component
Strong state-of-the-art results on HR-SOD benchmarks with 14.0%-17.1% improvement
Good reproducibility with detailed implementation details, hyperparameters, and computational cost specifications
Well-organized presentation with informative figures and clear methodology description
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Architecture from Ranftl et al. (2021), multi-mask decoding is standard, primarily combines existing techniques (FLUX, DINO-v3) without fundamental innovation
Evaluation artifacts: S3OD* metric uses 'best of 3 predicted masks' which may provide unfair advantage compared to single-output baselines, potentially inflating performance metrics

Incomplete ablation of multi-modal components: Table 6 shows effects but lacks deep analysis of which modalities contribute to specific performance gains; hyperparameter choices (α=8, β=0.5) appear empirically determined without principled justification
Insufficient domain gap analysis: Limited failure case examination, FID scores indicate remaining domain gap, no systematic analysis of object categories where method struggles

Dataset specification concerns: Object category coverage and distribution not clearly specified; reproducibility of synthetic generation requires specific models and substantial computational resources (H200 GPUs)
Narrow scope limited to salient object detection only: No evidence of generalization to other dense prediction tasks or broader computer vision applications
Methodological ambiguities: Quality filtering removes 6.8% of samples with limited analysis of filtered content; consistency threshold τ=0.8 and other hyperparameters appear arbitrary
Incomplete comparison with other synthetic data methods: Brief mentions of MaskFactory and DatasetDM without deep comparative analysis of why proposed multi-modal approach is superior
Missing diversity analysis: No explicit quantitative metrics for synthetic data diversity; unclear if long-tail object categories are adequately covered
Overclaimed generalization: Comparison between models trained on synthetic-only data versus real+synthetic data needs more careful interpretation to justify broad claims

strengths: Large-scale synthetic SOD dataset (139K+ images) substantially larger than existing datasets, will have significant practical value for the community
Comprehensive experimental validation across 6 benchmarks with strong cross-dataset generalization results (20-50% error reduction) and convincing zero-shot transfer to camouflaged object detection

Well-engineered multi-modal diffusion pipeline effectively combining FLUX DIT, DINO-v3, and concept attention for high-quality synthesis with rigorous 6-stage quality filtering achieving 6.8% rejection rate
Strong empirical results showing models trained only on synthetic data achieve competitive or superior performance to those trained on real data, with state-of-the-art results on multiple benchmarks
Rigorous quality control with Gemma-3 VLM assessment, semantic validation, and consistency filtering demonstrating higher quality than MaskFactory and other synthetic datasets
Good reproducibility documentation including implementation details, training time, computational requirements, and thoughtful ablation studies on architecture components and iterative generation
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty - primarily combines existing techniques (FLUX, DINO-v3, multi-choice learning) without introducing new losses, architectures, or algorithms; individual components are straightforward applications of prior work

Insufficient analysis of synthetic-to-real domain gap and reasons for effectiveness - lacks systematic study of which object categories/scene types generalize better, failure modes, or deep insights into why synthetic data outperforms expectations

Iterative generation mechanism may introduce bias toward specific object categories through category weight adaptation; parameters (α=8, β=0.5) appear arbitrary without sensitivity analysis or justification

Incomplete baseline comparisons under identical training conditions - many baseline results sourced from prior works with potentially different setups; limited comparison with other recent synthetic data generation methods and domain adaptation techniques

Missing critical ablations - no study of dataset size vs quality trade-offs, sensitivity to LLM prompts, necessity of individual diffusion model components, or justification for selecting specific FLUX layers [4,16,27,38]

Evaluation protocol concerns - baseline methods may not be retrained on identical datasets; risk of overfitting to benchmark characteristics used for iterative adaptation; zero-shot camouflaged object detection uses ground-truth real image masks

S3OD provides no train/test split since fully synthetic, limiting certain research directions; dataset release timing unclear; code availability stated as future work; potential biases from LLM prompts not analyzed

Incomplete technical justification - multi-mask decoder design lacks thorough motivation for SOD specifically; exponential decay weighting in loss function not clearly justified; smallest gains on DAVIS-S (Table 4) suggest domain-specific limitations

strengths: Large-scale synthetic dataset (139K+ images) addresses data scarcity in SOD and provides a valuable resource to the community
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple SOD benchmarks (DIS-SK, HR-SOD, UHRSD, DAVIS-S, DUT-OMRON) with detailed results tables and cross-dataset generalization studies
Thoughtful multi-stage quality filtering pipeline (consistency, mask quality, semantic validation) with demonstrated effectiveness (6.8% sample removal)
Well-motivated problem combining practical concerns about data scarcity with technical solutions using modern generative models
Multi-modal supervision combining FLUX DFT features, DINO-v3 representations, and attention maps provides interpretable training signals
Clear presentation with informative visualizations and extensive ablation studies demonstrating component contributions
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: multi-mask decoder is a straightforward extension of DFT, and the work primarily combines existing techniques (FLUX, DINO-v3, DFT) without significant innovation or modification
Incremental performance improvements: actual gains over baselines are modest (often single-digit percentage points in Tables 3 and 5); claims of '20-50% improvement' are not substantiated by results

Problematic evaluation design: the oracle evaluation (Table 4) using ground-truth masks is circular since the model is trained to match ground truth; the real test is fine-tuning (Table 5) where improvements are marginal

Weak justification for core design choice of multi-mask decoding versus single high-resolution mask; the connection between SOD ambiguity and multi-mask output lacks theoretical or empirical justification
Dataset quality concerns: despite filtering, Inception Score (35.19) and FID (1.74) indicate domain gap; only 0.7% of samples (1,000 of 139K) manually verified for correctness

Reproducibility challenges: heavy dependency on FLUX (12B parameters) and specific LLM versions for prompt generation; extensive computational requirements (8 H200 GPUs for 2 days); prompt strategy reproducibility unclear

Weak ablation results: iterative generation provides only 3.6% F-measure gain on DIS (Table 7) with no statistical significance testing; auxiliary loss and regularization design choices lack justification (λ_mask=10, γ=0.2)

Overstated generalization claims: method requires fine-tuning on target datasets to match state-of-the-art; zero-shot transfer limited to 3 COD benchmarks; unclear if the synthetic pre-training provides meaningful advantage beyond standard pre-training

Missing key comparisons: limited evaluation against recent synthetic data methods beyond MaskFactory; no comparison with data augmentation baselines or transfer learning approaches; no comparison of simple augmentation on small real datasets

Insufficient analysis: limited error analysis showing what types of errors synthetic data resolves; no failure case study; missing insights into why certain object categories benefit more from synthetic data

strengths: Large-scale dataset contribution (139,000+ images, >2x existing SOD datasets), addressing real annotation scarcity problem in dense prediction tasks
Comprehensive and rigorous evaluation across 8 diverse benchmarks with proper cross-dataset generalization testing and zero-shot domain transfer (COD)
Strong empirical results: models trained solely on synthetic data achieve state-of-the-art generalization with 20-50% MAE reduction vs. real-data baselines
Thoughtful engineering: iterative generation framework adaptively prioritizes challenging examples; multi-stage quality filtering; multi-mask decoder handling ambiguity
Thorough ablation studies (Tables 7-10, 15) validating design choices and demonstrating complementarity of feature modalities
Well-designed multi-modal supervision combining FLUX DFT features, DINO-v3 semantic features, and concept attention maps
Good reproducibility: clear implementation details, hyperparameters, dataset statistics provided
Practical impact demonstrating viability of synthetic data for dense prediction, addressing architectural bottleneck through feature complementarity
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: multi-mask decoder is straightforward extension; feature extraction uses existing models (DINO-v3); main contribution is thoughtful combination rather than novel techniques

Data quality concerns: only 0.1% of dataset manually verified with 1.4% error rate detected (suggesting ~1,946 total errors); 6.8% rejection in filtering pipeline; acknowledged unnatural images and boundary imprecision
Shallow analysis of model behavior: limited failure case investigation; minimal ablation on filtering thresholds; surface-level domain shift analysis (UMAP); missing statistical significance testing
Model architecture simplicity: multi-mask decoder lacks sophistication; relaxed assignment is standard practice; contribution is data-centric rather than learning-centric

Evaluation concerns: oracle evaluation using ground-truth at test time is methodologically questionable; 'zero-shot' COD evaluation misleading (pre-trained on SOD); baseline fairness affected by different training datasets
Limited generalization scope: primarily evaluated on similar SOD tasks; no evaluation on related tasks (instance/panoptic segmentation); cross-domain transfer shown only for COD
High computational cost: 2 days training on 8 H200 GPUs; FLUX inference at 25 steps per image; dataset generation cost unspecified; scalability unclear
Overstated claims: 'ambiguity-aware architecture' description inflates contribution; multi-mask selection is standard multi-hypothesis approach; dataset release contingent on unconfirmed commitment
